This is Frank Defratis, and welcome to HoloTalk, the Internet's laser and holography talk show enjoyed in over 42 countries throughout the world.
And now, here's this week's show.
Hello?
Hello, is this Martin?
Indeed it is.
How are you, Martin?
That's Frank Defrates.
Hey, Frank, I'm glad to hear from you.
Good.
How's everything going up there, okay?
Real good, real good.
I've been uh looking forward to our conversation.
I hope I have something interesting to convey.
Probably the best way to start all this out, having you talk a little bit about your work up there specifically, I imagine, is through Photon and Photon 2.
How long have you been involved with uh students teaching them about photonics and holography?
Okay.
First of all, let me say that Tantasqua regional high school where I teach is located in Sturbridge, Massachusetts.
Many of the listeners may be familiar roughly where that is, in central Massachusetts.
And the school serves five towns surrounding Sturbridge and has about twelve hundred students.
It has both an academic and a technical division.
And my program in photonics is officially vested in the technical division or what used to be called vocational division of many high schools.
And uh, however, is available also to academic students as a science elective in the school, and we'll talk a little bit more about what the classes and the courses are.

But broadly speaking, I got involved in this uh several years ago, about three years ago, when the director of Tantask was technical school and the head of the science department approached me while I was still in private industry and indicated that they had found some grant money and would I be willing to help them construct a high school level curriculum in photonics?
Mm-hmm.

Uh it turned out that I had already done a bit of that through my involvement with Project Photon, which some of the listeners may know as a national science Foundation sponsored effort through the New England Board of Higher Education to develop curricula for high school educators in subjects such as fiber optics and lasers and light in general.
Fiber fiber optics was actually your your main background at one time.
I mean it was, yes.
My uh my my my work over the last twenty-five years in industry has been in optical fibers, optical fiber materials, and the infrared uh optical materials.
Mm-hmm.
And this led to you going into the high schools when you were asked to run these programs.
That's correct.

I'm uh uh I can't say that I'm the uh youngest guy in the world, but this is one of these opportunities that comes along once in a lifetime to uh convey the uh experience and knowledge that you have to the next generation, if you will, and it's I must admit the uh best career move I probably have made.
Uh I wish I had done it fifteen years ago, to be honest.
Now holography entails a small portion of this this whole program.
I imagine there are a lot of other activities that you have going on centered around the field of photonics.
Are you preparing students for m for moving out into the workforce, for instance?
Uh they're indoctrinated into the realm of photonics through your high school and perhaps maybe move on to a four year college or even a technical college after they graduate from high school.
We do the program is aimed at doing all of those things.
First of all, we do train students for the world of work in the um traditional technical school sense.

Uh for example, I have students right now interning at some of the local fiber optic companies, and they use the training and the knowledge that they pick up in the photonics courses that they've taken through my program.

Simultaneously, since academic students can take this program on what we call the college preparatory or honors level, they can move on to a two or a four-year college program with uh at least sufficient knowledge so that they are familiar with broad photonic concepts with broad concepts in optics and optical physics and so that they at least know many of the buzz phrases and basic principles.
My intent has never been to try and graduate miniature electrical engineers from this program but to give students a a leg up whether they're going into the world of work or to college.

I know that the area that you're in is actually a hotbed for um photonics high tech education and at the four-year level, but uh how are things for uh high technologies, photonics uh in particular with your technical colleges?
Oh community college we have an extremely good program very close to us here.

I am uh uh not too far away about 45 minutes drive from Springfield uh Massachusetts and Springfield Technical Community College has an outstanding two year program in lasers and electro optic technology.

At the same time a lady named uh Professor Judy Donnelly teaches at uh Three Rivers Community College here in Connecticut about 45 minutes south and she teaches a similar program and indeed has done quite a bit of work uh retraining folks from um for example the electric boat division of general dynamics when there were large layoffs down there in the area of fiber optics and photonics.
What what's the interest like with the students?
Interest level is very high.

I guess it's I guess the honest answer is you uh get out of it what you put in, and thanks to um uh some of the uh things that you've had up on your website, the activities that you've conducted, holography, etc., uh we've been able to get the students uh fairly fired up.

I think uh you and I had communicated by email, and I mentioned to you the fact that uh my original plan in holography was to do it as a excuse me, uh, say one week activity or so, and it's turned into a two or three-week adventure uh because of the students' enthusiasm and interest.
That's wonderful.
Are are they following any uh particular path in high school?
Uh this isn't a technical high school, this is uh are these honor students?
The students that I have are both uh let me let me say this.
First of all, they are 10th, 11th, and 12th graders.
Okay.
They are generally on the college prep uh or honors level.
They are both technical and academic students.
And let me be clear so that the listeners understand what the nature of this program is.
The photonics technology program at Tantaspa consists of a series of courses.
They are one semester each, that is a half year.
They meet for 84 minutes each day.
So the kids get a lot of learning in that one semester.
The first course that they would take would be entitled Introduction to Light and Lasers, and that covers exactly what you think it does.
Basic photonics, what is light, what is lasers, how do they work, what are its applications?
And it is at that point that I introduce holography as a as a basic topic, and the students are taught how to make, process, create, and learn about reflection holography.
Yeah.
The second course that they take, the second semester is entitled Introduction to Fiber Optics.
And in that course, they learn about fiber optics, both telecommunications, fiber, and non-telecommunications applications of fibers, such as imaging, laser power transmission, sensors, etc.
And in that course, they gain both theoretical and practical knowledge.
They have to learn how to put connectors on fiber, they have to learn how to polish fiber, they have to learn how to measure fiber.
The third course in the series is entitled geometric and physical optics.
And in that course, we do more holography, transmission holography.
We also learn about optical instruments and the behavior of lenses and various optical elements.
Finally, we have some open courses in the sense that they uh teach students about principles of engineering.
We have a course entitled Exactly That Principles of Engineering.
So the um curriculum is quite varied.
That gives you a quick idea of the types of courses we have.
What are some of the actual experiments that they would conduct in the classroom environment?

Oh, well, for example, uh, they have to do everything from build and interpret uh a Michelson interferometer to understanding how a supermarket scanner works to learning uh how to do um optical time domain reflectometry measurements on fibers.
Uh they learn how to splice and cleave fibers.
I am blessed in the sense that local industry has been very kind to me with donations of equipment, and I have a very nice fusion splicer that the students can use.
Uh I have an OTDR that they can use.
They uh also get involved with uh building simple optical instruments, telescopes.
Uh, camera obscura is an exciting project that they did with uh some of the art departments in our school.
So there gives you a flavor.
That's an incredible preparatory course.

And to answer or assuage those uh concerns, we've gone out to actually other high schools in the area to attract new students, and we've also done a lot more publicity work inside the high school.
I do a couple of uh training or teaching days for all of our ninth grade students now, so that I'll hopefully get a new crop of tenth graders coming into the program.
Uh the other thing that we would like to do, I mentioned earlier in the conversation, and that's uh build the program up into uh to include more pre engineering type of activities.

We would like to create a engineering academy within Tantasqua High School that might have uh an admission exam and bring in a very high quality uh student that we could then uh train for uh admission to a four-year engineering school.
That would be fantastic.

The other thing, of course, to do is to keep on uh, and this is this is my little pitch here, is to keep on knocking on doors and hope that people will continue to be generous with their donations uh of equipment and uh parts.
Uh high schools aren't uh the first ones in line when industry thinks of giving stuff away, if you know what I mean.
Yeah, yeah, exactly.

We have about I have about uh 25% girls in my class, depending on what the course is.
Uh to be honest, it varies between like 15 and 25 percent.
Uh young ladies, uh I encourage very much because I feel strongly that women uh absolutely need to be better represented in the engineering uh disciplines, the engineering professions.

Yeah.

Okay.

No, it is not, it's relatively uh rural.
We are about uh sixty-five miles west of uh Boston.
Okay.
It certainly couldn't be considered a um suburb of Boston anyway.
It's sixty-five miles, yeah.
There there are some very interesting programs that are happening in rural areas compared to urban right now.
Yeah, yeah.

Shortly, shortly.

Uh at the moment, the best I can do for you is our um uh the little newsletter that I sent you that shows some pictures that we have taken and also has some photographs of my holographic setup.

It's uh WW uh NEBHE dot org.
New England Board of Higher Education.

We have been making both reflection and transmission holograms, and uh as as you know, I've had uh exceptionally good success now with the small uh uh diode laser unit that you uh uh supply people with.
Worked out uh very well indeed.

Oh, thank you very much.

Yeah, exactly.

Okay, now you have to set up all of your equipment in accordance with the instructions that we've had.
